questions.q: Who was the general that ended the Mauryan dynasty and established the Shunga dynasty?
questions.a: The general was Pushyamitra Shunga. A wrong answer here suggests the student is confusing the Shungas with the Mauryas or other later dynasties, showing a need to review the timeline of the end of the Mauryan rule.

questions.q: Why did the Mauryan Empire shrink after the death of Ashoka?
questions.a: It shrank because the successors who followed Ashoka were not as capable, making it difficult to keep the vast empire united. A wrong answer suggests the student believes empires always stay the same size, ignoring the role of leadership in governance.

questions.q: If you were a trader living in the northwest after the Mauryans declined, why might you see new people like the Indo-Greeks settling near you?
questions.a: You would see them because the Mauryan central army was no longer strong enough to hold the northwest border, allowing descendants of earlier Greek settlers to establish their own kingdoms. A wrong answer shows a failure to connect the decline of a central "superpower" with the rise of regional or foreign powers.

questions.q: Compare the size of the Shunga kingdom to the original Mauryan Empire based on the provided text.
questions.a: The Shunga kingdom was much smaller and mostly limited to the Ganga plain, unlike the vast Mauryan Empire that spanned almost the entire subcontinent. A wrong answer indicates the student hasn't grasped the concept of "territorial decline."

questions.q: Is it accurate to say that the entire Indian subcontinent was ruled by one single authority after 185 BCE? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, it is not accurate because the text describes a time when various kingdoms rose in different parts of the subcontinent, such as the Shungas in the Ganga plain and Indo-Greeks in the northwest. A wrong answer reveals a misconception that India's political history is a continuous, unbroken chain of one single empire.

questions.q: Imagine a map of India in 200 BCE vs 100 BCE. How would the boundaries change?
questions.a: The map in 200 BCE would show a large, singular block (Mauryan), while the map in 100 BCE would show a fragmented landscape with many small, distinct color-coded regions. A poor answer ignores the shift from a centralized state to a decentralized one.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The Post-Mauryan period refers to the era following the decline of the Mauryan Empire (around 185 BCE), ______ by the rise of smaller, regional kingdoms like the Shungas and the influence of Indo-Greek rulers in the northwest.
Fill in the blank: Imagine your school team, which was once the largest and strongest in the city, suddenly loses its head coach and begins to break into smaller, ______ clubs.

Fill in the blank: The Post-Mauryan period refers to the era following the decline of the Mauryan Empire (around ______ BCE), characterized by the rise of smaller, regional kingdoms like the Shungas and the influence of Indo-Greek rulers in the northwest.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to identify that the Mauryan Empire did not vanish instantly but transformed into several smaller regional powers and explain that the transition involved both internal political shifts and external foreign influences.
